the AML1–ETS gene rearrangement can be detected in the majority of cases of AML with t (8;21) by RQ-PCR, that the levels of the AML1 – ETS transcript are variable at diagnosis, and that the quantitative analysis of this transcript can identify patients at high risk of relapse after therapy.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the level of AML1-ETO transcript in PB or BM samples can be used as a predictor of relapse risk in patients with AML and t(8; 21).
the monitoring of MRD by RQ-PCR is an early predictive factor for the relapse risk.
